recommended_change.label: full-tuning-mitigations-off
host_commands:
cat > /etc/systemd/system/dnswait.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
exec >/var/tmp/dnswait.log 2>&1
set -x
boot=$(( $(date +%s) - $(cut -d. -f1 /proc/uptime) ))
for i in $(seq 1 90); do
  s=$(stat -c %Y /var/tmp/startup-5.status 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
  [ "$s" -gt "$boot" ] && break
  sleep 5
done
sleep 5
cp -a /var/local/bindbak/. /etc/bind/
ethtool -G eno4 rx 2040; sleep 5
for q in /sys/class/net/eno4/queues/rx-*; do echo ff > $q/rps_cpus; done
sysctl -w net.core.netdev_max_backlog=30000 net.core.rmem_max=16777216 net.core.rmem_default=16777216
ethtool -C eno4 rx-usecs 200 rx-frames 128 rx-usecs-irq 200 rx-frames-irq 128
ethtool -K eno4 gro off
for i in 0 1 2 3 4 5 6 7; do printf '%x' $((1<<i)) > /sys/class/net/eno4/queues/tx-$i/xps_cpus; done
sysctl -w net.core.default_qdisc=pfifo_fast
tc qdisc replace dev eno4 root handle 1: mq
sysctl -w net.ipv4.conf.all.rp_filter=0 net.ipv4.conf.eno4.rp_filter=0 net.ipv4.conf.default.rp_filter=0
echo always > /sys/kernel/mm/transparent_hugepage/enabled
tc qdisc show dev eno4; ethtool -c eno4; cat /proc/cmdline; wc -l /etc/bind/db.workbench.lan
exit 0
EOF

recommended_apply_script:

test $(wc -l < /etc/bind/db.workbench.lan) -gt 60000
sed -i 's/^GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX_DEFAULT=""/GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX_DEFAULT="mitigations=off"/' /etc/default/grub

mkdir -p /etc/systemd/system/ssh.service.d
printf '[Service]\nExecStartPre=-/etc/systemd/system/dnswait.sh\nTimeoutStartSec=900\n' > /etc/systemd/system/ssh.service.d/zz-wait.conf
systemctl daemon-reload

sudo systemctl reboot
summary:
RECOMMENDATION: full-tuning-mitigations-off (240k QPS; baseline 150k, +60%).
Settings: kernel cmdline mitigations=off; RPS on all 8 CPUs for every eno4 rx queue (rps_cpus=ff); netdev_max_backlog=30000; rmem_max/rmem_default=16 MB plus BIND "udp-receive-buffer 16777216;"; eno4 rx ring 2040; RX coalescing rx-usecs/rx-usecs-irq 200, rx-frames/rx-frames-irq 128; GRO off; XPS cpu i -> tx-i; pfifo_fast instead of fq_codel under mq; rp_filter=0; THP=always.

CONFIDENCE: high for 240k. This config and two variants that only added things passed 240k in 4 of 4 reboot runs (99.84, 99.51, 99.84, 99.996%) and failed 250k in all four (96.4-97.8%). The baseline was 150k both times it was measured, so noise between runs is small compared with the 10k step. No-reboot fallback: best230-thp-coal200, the same tuning without mitigations=off, kept Spectre/Meltdown protections. It passed 230k and 240k (240k at 99.36%) and is about 1-1.5% slower at 250k (95-96%). Use it if disabling CPU mitigations is not acceptable. In production, persist the tuning with a systemd unit, sysctl.d and GRUB.

WHAT LIMITS THE SERVER (measured):
1. Baseline: bnx2 (BCM5709, 1 GbE) RSS hashes UDP on IP addresses only. All traffic from the single client lands on one RX queue and one CPU, and that CPU runs out at about 150k. No NIC drops; the losses were UDP RcvbufErrors. rx-flow-hash and ntuple are not supported. RPS fixed this: 200k.
2. After RPS the server is purely CPU-bound. I sampled /proc/stat during runs. At about 230k all 8 logical CPUs (4C/8T Xeon E5530, Nehalem, 2.4 GHz) are about 100% busy: about 69% user (named), 18% sys, 13% softirq. The CPU taking the RX IRQ spends 40-50% in softirq. Losses are only socket-buffer overflow, with no NIC or backlog drops. Under overload, receive livelock (dropped packets still cost protocol processing) makes answered QPS sag slightly.
3. A perf profile shows BIND user time spread flat over hundreds of functions: ns__client_setup, dns_qp_lookup, message parse/render, compression, stats counters and so on. It costs about 23 us of CPU time per query per hyperthread, with no hotspot a config option can remove. Kernel per-packet work is also spread out.
4. What helped: RPS (+33%). Coalescing 12->64/128 frames plus GRO off (+~8%), which batches NAPI polls and cuts RPS IPIs. XPS + pfifo_fast + rp_filter off (+~4%). THP + coalescing 200/128 (+~1-2%). mitigations=off (+~1.5-3%; Nehalem lacks PCID, but the measured gain was small).
5. What did not help (no difference): performance governor plus disabling deep C-states; RFS; TX coalescing; psi=0; stopping irqbalance; unloading named's AppArmor profile; sched_migration_cost/autogroup tweaks.

PROCESS NOTES / CAVEATS:
- On every boot, Emulab's profile startup re-clones /local/repository and re-runs ns_software/bind/install.sh. That copies the stub zone files and the default named.conf.options over /etc/bind, so the 65k-record db.workbench.lan becomes an 11-line stub. It also races with the harness. This caused one failed run and one 0-QPS run. It also corrupts the server after every restore reboot, because the restore happens before the startup runs and residual_drift does not report it. I worked around it: an ssh.service ExecStartPre waits for the startup to finish, then puts back /etc/bind and applies the tuning. Every later config first re-extracts the zone from /var/tmp/agent_baseline.tgz. Anyone doing reboot experiments here should know this.
- Leftover drift: the root mq was rebuilt but its child qdiscs stayed pfifo_fast (the restore only checks the root qdisc). I fixed it with a final baseline repeat (150k), and checked afterwards that eno4 has mq + 8x fq_codel, the zone is the full 65,546 lines, and the kernel cmdline is stock. linux-tools (perf) was installed for profiling and is still installed; it does not affect performance. Three measurements were left unused because no remaining knob looked able to add the ~2-3% needed to pass 250k.

NEXT STEPS: the remaining headroom is in named's CPU cost, not in tuning. Options: a NIC with real UDP 4-tuple RSS (removes RPS/IPI overhead and the RX-CPU hotspot); a newer CPU; or a lighter authoritative server (Knot/NSD are typically 2-4x more efficient per query than BIND).
